reasons: The finding correctly identifies § 12.4 as a Customer-binding non-compete with undefined scope ('any product or service that competes'), worldwide territory, and a 24-month post-term tail — squarely within the rule's walk-away band, so 'deviation' at high severity is right.

The redline deletes p0050 in full, which is exactly the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer) and the minimal edit that reaches it; no residual restriction remains and deterministic checks confirm this.

The comment is accurate: it states what was removed, notes the direct contradiction with § 12.3 (which confirms no non-compete/exclusivity commitment), cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (single named product, term only, 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) without lecturing.

Tone and prefix conform to instructions (concise, first person plural, '[Playbook]' prefix); the high changed-character ratio is justified because the rule requires deleting the offending obligation rather than rewording it.
